```{=html}
<div class="hero-banner">
  <div class="hero-eyebrow">System identification for LIGO suspensions</div>
  <h1 class="hero-title">
    Spend the measurement budget<br>
    <span class="hero-accent">where the model is least certain.</span>
  </h1>
  <p class="hero-subtitle">
    A flat broadband injection spends drive power uniformly, including on
    frequencies where the model is already well constrained.
    <strong style="color:rgba(255,255,255,0.92);">system_ident</strong>
    implements the Pintelon–Schoukens method end to end: given a prior model and a
    fixed drive-power budget, it estimates where each Hz of bandwidth contributes
    the most Fisher information, lays a low-crest periodic multisine there,
    measures the response leakage-free, fits the plant by maximum likelihood
    toward the Cramér–Rao bound, and repeats — with Tukey ramps and an operator
    STOP for safe injection.
  </p>
```

::: {.column-screen-inset style="max-width:980px; margin:1.5rem auto 0;"}

Press **Play** to watch the Pintelon–Schoukens fixed-point iteration reshape a flat drive
into the Fisher-optimal excitation, concentrating power near the resonance where each Hz
contributes the most information.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: true
#| warning: false
import sys, pathlib
_p = pathlib.Path.cwd()
for _c in [_p, *_p.parents]:
    for _d in (_c, _c / "docs"):
        if (_d / "sysid_plots.py").exists() and str(_d) not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, str(_d))
import numpy as np
import sysid_plots as sp
from system_ident.model import TFModel
from system_ident.design.pintelon import optimal_excitation
from system_ident.fisher import parameter_covariance

freq   = np.linspace(0.1, 4.0, 600)
model  = TFModel.from_resonances([(1.0, 20.0)], gain=1.0)
Pyy, Px_tot = np.ones_like(freq), 1.0
resp = np.abs(model.eval(freq))

# every fixed-point iteration, flat -> Fisher-optimal (one call records them all)
Pxx_rec, _, _ = optimal_excitation(freq, model, Pyy, Px_tot, n_iter=8, rec_progress=True)
flat = np.full_like(freq, Px_tot / (freq[-1] - freq[0]))
asd_iters = [np.sqrt(flat)] + [np.sqrt(p) for p in Pxx_rec]

cov_opt  = parameter_covariance(freq, model, Pxx_rec[-1], Pyy, 256.0)
cov_flat = parameter_covariance(freq, model, flat,        Pyy, 256.0)
ratio    = np.max(np.diag(cov_flat)) / np.max(np.diag(cov_opt))

fig = sp.animate_design(freq, resp, asd_iters, height=470)
fig.update_layout(title=dict(
    text=f"<b>The optimal drive forming</b>  —  {ratio:.0f}× lower parameter variance than a flat sweep",
    x=0.5, xanchor="center", y=0.98))
fig.show()
```

```{=html}
<div class="page-section">
  <p class="section-label">Why it works</p>
  <div class="feature-grid">

    <div class="feature-card">
      <span class="feature-icon">&#119979;</span>
      <h3>Fisher-optimal excitation</h3>
      <p>The dispersion function ν(f) tells you how much each frequency bin contributes to
         parameter information given the current drive and readout noise.
         The Pintelon–Schoukens fixed-point iteration redistributes drive power toward
         high-ν bins under a fixed total-power budget — converging to the optimal spectrum
         in 3–5 iterations.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="feature-card">
      <span class="feature-icon">&#128257;</span>
      <h3>Leakage-free measurement, ML fit</h3>
      <p>The periodic multisine makes the response DFT leakage-free — a sharp resonance is
         measured at its true peak with no near-resonance bias. A reference-based,
         ratio-of-averages FRF cancels the controller in closed loop, and the Gaussian
         maximum-likelihood estimator turns it into model parameters at the Cramér–Rao
         bound. Passes accumulate by inverse-variance weighting, so broadband coverage is
         never thrown away, only enriched.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="feature-card">
      <span class="feature-icon">&#9741;</span>
      <h3>Safe injection</h3>
      <p>The multisine carries low-crest <strong>Schroeder phases</strong>, so a
         saturation-limited actuator delivers more in-band power for a fixed peak.
         Every waveform is Tukey-windowed (configurable ramp), keeping the actuation
         envelope within budget at startup and teardown. The watchdog monitors actuator
         and RMS levels every read segment; a breach or operator STOP triggers a
         safe handoff.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="feature-card">
      <span class="feature-icon">&#9881;</span>
      <h3>Same API — twin today, hardware next</h3>
      <p>The loop code never sees actuator channels or frame data directly — it speaks
         the <code>ChannelBackend</code> abstraction. <code>TwinBackend</code> runs the
         full campaign on a digital plant model today; a CDS hardware backend
         (<code>awg</code> inject + <code>nds2</code> readback) drops in behind the same
         interface, selected by one config line. That <code>CDSBackend</code> is
         currently a <strong>stub</strong> — the interface exists, the control-room
         implementation is in progress.</p>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
```
